lines: ReproPilot is for open source maintainers who get bug reports without a test. It turns a report into a failing test and a fix, and it runs both before it reports anything.
It was built for the Nebius and NVIDIA hackathon, in the Coding and Agentic Engineering track, on Nemotron models from Nebius Token Factory.
Here is the bundled example. A batching helper called chunked silently drops the last, smaller batch.
Most bug reports look like this. There is a description and a snippet, but no test.
The agent copies the code into a fresh workspace, and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning triages the report.
Then Nemotron 3.5 Super writes a reproduction test, and the test is executed.
The test fails on an assertion that matches the report. The last batch, with the number five, is missing.
Only a failure like that counts. If a test passed, or broke on an import error, the real output would go back to the model for another try.
Here is the test the model wrote. In this run the first attempt was accepted.
Next comes the patch. The fix is a one line change to the range inside chunked.
A patch is kept only if the new test passes and the full suite still passes. All seven tests pass.
The result is a unified diff, the run logs, and a pull request description that is ready to paste.
Model calls go to NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory, through its OpenAI compatible API.
A Sandboxes runner can run each test in its own virtual machine. It waits on beta access, so this run used the local runner.
Everything in this recording is a real run. The answers came from Nemotron, and the tests ran with pytest. The whole run took about ten seconds.
The hosted page replays that run. The code is open source under the MIT license.
